commands.name: audit-plan
commands.description: Audit a plan/design/spec doc that describes how to parse an external data format (JSONL transcripts, API responses, wire protocols, file formats), forcing every content-shape claim to be backed by a real sample dump — not memory, not analogous formats, not "it should look like X". Use when the user runs /audit-plan <doc> to break the recurring "each review round catches one unverified content type" failure pattern. Do not use for plain code review within one's own codebase, or docs describing already-implemented behavior (verified by reading the implementation).

commands.name: exec-plan
commands.description: Drive a plan document (docs/…, plan.md, roadmap) to completion as a durable, proof-carrying task queue persisted under .exec-plan/state/. Use when the user wants to execute or resume a phased plan across sessions, enforce impl+tests+regression gating backed by real evidence, audit whether "done" tasks are actually proven, or auto-generate an audit-ready completion report. Do not use for one-off bug fixes, plain code review, or ad-hoc todo management without a plan file.

commands.name: handoff-doc
commands.description: Generate a standardized handoff document under the project's handoffs/ directory so another agent or a future session can continue the work without losing context. Use when the user wants a session handoff, transfer note, or resumable context package. Automatically preserves active exec-plan state (plan / queue / resume command) when present. Use when the user runs /handoff-doc.

commands.name: ios-real-device-doc
commands.description: Create or upgrade repo-aware iOS real-device testing docs, regression checklists, and validation runbooks. Use this whenever the user asks for a 真机测试方案文档, 测试 checklist, backend validation guide, XCUITest runbook, QA/回归文档, or wants a doc another agent can follow on a connected iPhone without extra explanation. Always use it when the doc must include preflight steps, device detection/UDID, launchctl/port checks, blocked vs N/A rules, automation gate order, existing smoke UITest or launch-hook reuse, service/backend selection, evidence requirements, acceptance-log templates, or an honest automation-gap analysis that should not need a later rewrite.

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. On Grok Build, prefer this for full create/eval/iterate loops; use /create-skill only for a minimal one-shot scaffold.

commands.name: supervise
commands.description: Audit a development agent's work against a design doc's roadmap, issue numbered 监工指令 directives, and verify completion reports independently. Use when the user wants you to act as supervisor over another agent's implementation work — issuing "监工指令 N 号" directives, preventing roadmap drift, or auditing whether claimed-complete work actually meets the design framework. Use when the user runs /supervise <doc>, says "你当监工", "审计开发 agent", "下发监工指令", or pastes a developer agent's completion report for verification. Do not use for direct implementation, code review without a design doc, one-off bug fixes, or when you are yourself the implementation agent.

commands.name: takeover
commands.description: Read a handoff document, rebuild working context, validate it against the current project state, and continue the task immediately. Use when the user wants to resume work from a saved handoff file or asks an agent to take over a previous session. When the handoff carries exec-plan context, resumes the correct next exec-plan action automatically. Use when the user runs /takeover.

commands.name: design

commands.name: execute-plan
commands.description: Execute a PR Plan DAG from a design document. Parses the plan, topologically sorts it, implements PRs in parallel using worktree-isolated subagents, runs mandatory orchestrator-level review, and assembles either a Graphite PR stack or a plain-git branch stack depending on tool availability.

commands.name: implement
commands.description: Run the full implement-review-fix loop using implementer and reviewer personas. Supports effort-based multi-reviewer scaling (1-5 reviewers) with automatic specialization selection. Includes memory-based feedback loop that learns from past review patterns. Loops until all reviewers find 0 issues of any severity.

commands.name: long-running-background-tasks
commands.description: Required reading before you start, watch, or wait on anything that keeps running after you launch it — background jobs, watchers, scheduled loops, CI, pull requests, training runs, dev servers, long builds. Read it before you launch such work and before you report on its state. Saying where a running job stands counts as working on it. Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.

commands.name: pr-babysit
commands.description: Monitor PRs, fix CI failures, address review comments, resolve merge conflicts, and restack stacks. Supports independent PRs, Graphite stacks, and GitHub stacked PRs (gh-stack).
